short: Passed the civil rights laws of the century and lost his presidency in Vietnam.
full:
Johnson took the oath aboard the presidential aircraft at Dallas and used the shock of the assassination, along with thirty years of legislative craft, to force through the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965. His Great Society added Medicare, Medicaid, federal aid to schools, immigration reform and the war on poverty, the largest expansion of domestic government since the New Deal.

He also escalated in Vietnam. American strength rose from about 16,000 advisers to more than half a million troops, authorised by the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution of August 1964 on the basis of a second attack that probably never occurred. The Tet Offensive of January 1968 destroyed public confidence in official accounts of the war. On 31 March 1968 Johnson announced he would not seek another term.
